name: ai-harness

verification.note: Bundled profile-resolution.json ships unresolved until profiles are chosen and resolved.

knownConstraints: Bundled web/React/Next scaffold and workflows are optional; remove unused paths if not selected.
Stack-specific rules generate only when matching profiles are active or proposed.
Local human approval records require protected branches and external environment controls.
Production release workflow verifies approval but does not deploy by itself.
New-repository bootstrap creates only the harness npm substrate and does not approve a product stack or lifecycle transition.

Codex project trust is user-scoped and is never auto-written; codex:preflight must confirm effective repo-local config plus current project hook discovered, enabled, and trusted before delegated ai:* commands.
GitHub context requires an intended HTTPS origin and reports bounded unavailability reason codes without stderr or tokens.
Cursor CLI is optional; live provider authentication and permission behavior must be verified on a workstation with the CLI installed.

Cursor security-critical preToolUse hooks are fail-closed. Complementary layered controls are CLI permissions, IDE approvals, sandbox/worktree isolation, and hook policy; explicit non-implementer CLI roles are write-denied, while an unset or empty role identifies an interactive IDE session.
Directory-scoped generated AGENTS.md files are retired; Codex specialization uses CODEX.md while Cursor uses scoped .mdc rules.

Planning seed documents have canonical copies under harness/templates/planning; harness tests read those templates directly while live docs/product and docs/architecture files remain mutable project state after bootstrap.
CodeRabbit GitHub App is optional and advisory; the core lifecycle works without it, repository configuration is canonical in .coderabbit.yaml, and it does not replace Codex independent review.

The distribution ships a private harness npm substrate (package.json + package-lock.json) so post-root CI can reach ready. Overlaying onto an existing application must merge fragments and must not overwrite that application's package metadata; when package.json name is not ai-harness, verify:harness checks the fragment merge instead of exact substrate identity.
deployment/aws records AWS hosting intent only; it does not create an AWS account, IAM principal, cloud resource, or deployment, and it does not add AWS SDK/CLI to the harness substrate.

cursorCli.primarySafetyBoundary: layered project permissions, fail-closed policy hook, approval, and harness-managed Git-common-dir worktree isolation
